errorMessage: A Chat Model sub-node must be connected and enabled
plainLanguageMeaning: Your AI Agent has no 'brain' attached. An AI Agent node can't run on its own — it needs a language model (like an OpenAI or Anthropic chat model) plugged into it, and that model node has to be turned on.

causes.title: No Chat Model sub-node connected to the AI Agent
causes.explanation: The AI Agent was added (or its model was removed) without a chat-model sub-node wired into the 'Chat Model' connector underneath it. This is the primary cause.

causes.title: A Chat Model is connected but disabled
causes.explanation: The model sub-node exists but was deactivated (greyed out), so the agent still sees no usable model.

fixSteps.instruction: With the AI Agent node open, click the '+ Chat Model' button at the bottom of the screen. With the node closed, click the 'Chat Model' + connector underneath it.
Pick a chat model provider (e.g. OpenAI Chat Model, Anthropic Chat Model) from the list n8n shows.
Open that chat-model sub-node, add or select valid credentials for the provider, and choose a model.
Make sure the chat-model sub-node is enabled (not greyed out). If it's deactivated, right-click it and choose 'Activate'.

whyItHappens: n8n's AI Agent is a 'root node' in a cluster: it orchestrates but delegates the actual text generation to a connected Chat Model sub-node. Before running, n8n checks that at least one enabled node is connected to the agent's required Chat Model input; deactivated sub-nodes don't count. If none is found, it stops with this error before any API request is made.
